rationale: While structural central nervous system anomalies—predominantly corpus callosum dysgenesis/thinning, ventriculomegaly, and cerebral/cerebellar volume loss—are bona fide features of DHX9-associated neurodevelopmental disorder (OMIM #620988), the specific quantitative claim that these findings occur in 'approximately 40-60% of patients who undergo neuroimaging' is entirely unsupported by the provided literature. The available sources document structural anomalies qualitatively in cohorts and case series (e.g., Calame et al., 2023; Dawidziuk et al., 2021) and report 2/2 (100%) in PanelApp curation data, but none provide evidence establishing a 40-60% frequency in imaged individuals.

evidence.text: Brain MRI of individuals with pathogenic monoallelic DHX9 variants demonstrated structural central nervous system anomalies including thin corpus callosum, enlargement of the ventricles, and cerebellar atrophy across affected individuals.

new_directions.question_text: What is the true penetrance and spectrum of neuroradiological abnormalities among all molecularly confirmed DHX9 patients who have undergone brain MRI?
new_directions.rationale: Existing cohorts are small and report qualitative findings (thin corpus callosum, ventriculomegaly, cerebellar/cerebral atrophy) or small subsets (2/2), leaving the true unbiased neuroimaging frequency unmeasured.
